tasks.short: Report market changes and purchasing costs to support sourcing and budget decisions.

steps.what: Export purchase prices, volumes, open orders and supplier terms.
Read market publications and supplier notices for relevant price and availability changes.

loop.input: Approved market publications and supplier notices.
loop.output: Dated market notes with categories, units and source passages.
loop.check: Require source passages; validate dates, currencies and units; flag conflicting claims.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per document; unreadable or conflicting material goes to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Relevant changes appear in varied prose and document layouts.

steps.what: Normalize prices and calculate category cost movements against previous periods and budgets.
Judge which changes matter and distinguish price effects from purchasing mix changes.
Write the report, explain cost drivers and check recommendations before circulation.

loop.input: Validated cost analysis, reviewed market notes and manager's report conclusions.
loop.output: Report draft with sourced commentary and fixed-format tables.
loop.check: Render figures directly from validated data; require citations and manager approval of commentary.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported explanations remain blank for the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: The narrative must connect changing market evidence with the manager's conclusions.

steps.what: Circulate the approved report to buyers, finance and budget holders.

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} joins exports from the {PROCUREMENT} and {ERP}, checks units and currencies, and produces cost tables in the {BI}. Bounded loops extract cited market notes and draft commentary in the {DOCS}; the purchasing manager selects conclusions and approves circulation through the {WORKFLOW} and {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Category mappings, inconsistent units and changing document formats made recurring reports costly to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort to build mappings, checks and report templates. Bounded extraction and drafting can handle prose while calculations remain deterministic.
tasks.still_hard: Comparable market data may require licences. Rebates, currency exposure and purchasing mix can make apparent price movements misleading.
tasks.human_edge: The manager understands supplier credibility, substitution options and when a market signal warrants changing purchasing plans.

ambition.what: Weekly purchasing-window review for volatile categories.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling reports and more time testing buying windows with buyers and finance. They can propose weekly changes; budget and contract authority remain subject to existing delegation.

reach.task: Compare supplier quotations using landed cost.
reach.learn: Freight, rebates, currency treatment and comparable specifications.

reach.task: Adjust category purchasing plans to demand and margin changes.
reach.learn: Sell-through, stock exposure and category margin drivers.

evidence.claim: Structured purchase records support deterministic normalization, calculations and report generation.
Bounded extraction can produce cited market notes, but commercial interpretation needs review.
Build ranges and remaining-time percentages are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: The company uses the {PROCUREMENT} and {ERP}; a workbook currently joins their reporting outputs.
Reports recur by category and use a reasonably stable template.
Time shares describe a typical report cycle and require validation.
The design processes commercial data and does not score employees.
Access follows GDPR where supplier contacts are personal data; consultation under national rules is included if the implementation changes employee monitoring.
unknowns: Available exports or interfaces and their access restrictions.
Market-data licences and permitted automated processing.
Category mappings, rebate treatment and currency conventions.
Report recipients, approval requirements and purchasing delegation.
Applicable national consultation requirements and internal access lead times.
research_questions: Which licensed market sources permit scheduled retrieval and text extraction?
Can native reporting in the {PROCUREMENT} and {ERP} replace parts of the proposed integration?
Which reconciliation checks best separate price changes from volume and mix effects?
new_work: Review extracted market claims and unsupported report commentary.
Resolve missing units, stale prices and unmatched categories.
Maintain category mappings, report templates and source access.
Check whether weekly signals improve purchasing decisions.

tasks.short: Choose and coordinate approved routes for returning, reusing, selling or recycling surplus materials.

steps.what: Identify surplus quantities, ownership, book values and stock locations.
Inspect quantities and condition, and flag handling or disposal restrictions.
Ask internal teams whether they can reuse the available materials.
Compare reuse, supplier return, resale and recycling routes using quotes and restrictions.
Approve the route, recipient, quantities, costs and any required write-off.
Confirm the approved arrangement and book collection or internal transfer.
Verify the collector and materials before release, then obtain collection evidence.
Check collection evidence and disposal certificates against the approved plan.

loop.input: Collection notes and disposal certificates in varied document formats.
loop.output: Evidence fields with document references and a comparison to the approved disposal plan.
loop.check: Match recipient, material, quantity and date; require source references and review discrepancies.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per document; missing or contradictory evidence goes to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: External evidence arrives as scans and documents without a common schema.

steps.what: Reconcile proceeds or fees and post approved stock and financial adjustments.

tasks.design: Configure a disposal case in the {WORKFLOW}, populated from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP}, with internal reuse requests and a deterministic comparison of route costs. The budget holder authorizes a specific plan before bookings through the {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}; changed terms require renewed approval, and warehouse staff approve physical release. A bounded document loop prepares the evidence pack in the {DOCS}, then finance reviews configured adjustments in the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Disposal is infrequent, involves physical condition checks and crosses stock, finance and external paperwork.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approval flows can hold a shared case. AI-assisted coding makes the small integrations and cost comparisons cheaper; bounded extraction reduces certificate paperwork.
tasks.still_hard: Physical condition, hazardous-material restrictions, recipient eligibility and resale value need case-specific judgement. External collectors may still coordinate by phone.
tasks.human_edge: People assess whether material is safe and useful, choose defensible recipients and stop an unsuitable release.

ambition.what: Internal project teams receive a searchable offer of reusable surplus materials.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time chasing bookings and documents and more time finding reuse routes. They can propose transfers across teams; disposal and write-off authority remain with the delegated approvers.

reach.task: Maintain disposal cases and chase missing collection evidence.
reach.learn: Evidence requirements, stock references and exception routing.

reach.task: Assess supplier return terms and obtain disposal quotes.
reach.learn: Return credits, transport costs and recipient qualification.

evidence.claim: Configured approval flows can coordinate disposal records, bookings and accounting handoffs.
Physical inspections and irreversible material releases retain human decision points.
Document extraction can support evidence matching but cannot establish recipient eligibility by itself.
Build ranges and remaining-time percentages are planning estimates, not documented disposal-case results.

assumptions: The task covers arranging disposal, including approval and closure, rather than performing transport or treatment.
The company holds stock records in the {OPS_SYSTEM} and financial values in the {ERP}.
The disposal policy specifies delegated approvals and required evidence.
The booking gate reuses the approval from s5 only while recipient, quantities, route and costs remain within that plan.
The reduction in s4 comes from prepared cost comparisons; the route decision stays human.
GDPR applies to personal contact data. Consultation under national rules is included if the implementation changes employee monitoring.
unknowns: Material types, condition and hazardous-material restrictions.
Permitted recipients, required certificates and retention periods.
Approval thresholds and authority for stock adjustments and write-offs.
Available interfaces, booking channels and identity checks at collection.
Whether internal reuse has enough demand to justify a searchable offer.
Applicable national consultation requirements and access lead times.
research_questions: Which native features in the {PROCUREMENT} and {WORKFLOW} support disposal cases and internal transfers?
Which environmental and transport requirements apply to each material and destination?
Can frequent collectors provide structured collection and treatment evidence?
new_work: Maintain disposal routes, approval thresholds and recipient records.
Handle changed booking terms and obtain renewed approval.
Review extracted certificates and chase missing evidence.
Resolve stock, quantity and accounting discrepancies.
Maintain the internal surplus offer and remove unavailable materials.

role.altitude: The purchasing manager's week shifts from report assembly and disposal coordination toward category choices, supplier discussions and reuse decisions. New tools support more frequent recommendations; formal spending, release and write-off rights change only through explicit delegation.
reach: Purchasing agents: quotation comparison and supplier return terms.
Wholesale and retail buyers: demand, margin and stock exposure.
Procurement clerks: evidence completeness and transaction closure.
skills_to_grow: Validate category data and distinguish price effects from purchasing mix.
Read sourced market evidence and test purchasing scenarios.
Evaluate reuse and disposal routes using costs, condition and restrictions.
Design approval thresholds and resolve cross-system exceptions.
role.ambitious_version: Run a weekly category cost review and an internal surplus reuse service, bringing specific purchasing and transfer proposals to the existing decision makers.
